name: RES4SHO arctangent two-stage schedules (atan_*)
plain: A bong_tangent-style two-stage schedule: stage 1 runs from the model's top sigma down to the linear midpoint, stage 2 from there to the bottom sigma, each shaped by an arctangent curve. Stage 1's pivot sits at its far end and stage 2's at its start, so steps are dense near σ_max and σ_min and sparse around the midpoint, with one large jump across it. atan_gentle, atan_focused and atan_steep use slope 0.15, 0.25 and 0.40 in both stages; atan_structure uses 0.10 then 0.35 and atan_detail 0.35 then 0.10. In our own check at 20 steps on an SD-range model, atan_structure put more of its late steps near σ_min than atan_detail did, so the names may not match the effect you expect. Surprises shared by the whole family: a request for N steps returns N+1 steps (n = N+2 minus one junction value, plus a trailing 0); the split point is the linear midpoint of σ_max..σ_min with 60% of the steps above it, so on SD-style models (σ_max about 14.6) most steps sit above σ≈7.3; slopes are divided by n/40, so the shape changes with step count. Registered with use_ms=True; names already in the scheduler table are skipped, not overwritten.
math:
Symbols: N requested steps; σ_max, σ_min from the model; n = N + 2; m = int(0.6 n); σ_mid = σ_min + 0.5(σ_max − σ_min) (linear midpoint).
Stage 1: k = 0..m−1, pivot p1 = m, slope s1' = s1/max(n/40, 0.1); Stage 2: k = 0..n−m−1, pivot p2 = 0, slope s2' = s2/max(n/40, 0.1).
Each stage: r_k = curve(k; p, s'); r̂_k = (r_k − r_last)/(r_first − r_last); σ_k = end + r̂_k (start − end), stage 1 from σ_max to σ_mid, stage 2 from σ_mid to σ_min.
Output = stage 1 without its last value, stage 2, then 0: N+2 values, i.e. N+1 steps.
curve(k; p, s) = ((2/π)·atan(−s(k − p)) + 1)/2.
Slopes (s1, s2): gentle (0.15, 0.15), focused (0.25, 0.25), steep (0.40, 0.40), structure (0.10, 0.35), detail (0.35, 0.10).

props.params: fixed by name; no inputs beyond steps
props.prints: draws an ASCII plot of the schedule to the console on every call
